name: Oseltamivir
summary: Oral neuraminidase inhibitor for influenza A and B; reduces illness duration and complications when started early.
mechanism: Inhibits influenza neuraminidase, preventing release of new virions from infected cells.
pharmacodynamics: Blocks viral spread within the respiratory tract; greatest benefit when started within 48 hours of symptom onset.

pharmacokinetics.bioavailability: Prodrug — well absorbed; ~75% converted to the active carboxylate

dosing.adult: 75 mg PO every 12 hours for 5 days (treatment); 75 mg PO once daily (prophylaxis)
dosing.renalAdjustment: Reduce dose if CrCl < 30 mL/min (e.g. 30 mg once daily for treatment)

safety.pregnancy: Preferred agent for influenza in pregnancy (pregnant women are high risk)
warnings: Resistance (e.g. H275Y in seasonal H1N1) can limit effectiveness

indications: Influenza A and B — treatment started within 48 hours of symptom onset
clinicalPearls: Benefit is greatest when started within 48 hours of symptoms (reduces duration by ~1 day)
Not a substitute for annual influenza vaccination
good: Reduces influenza duration and complications, including in hospitalized and high-risk patients.
bad: Narrow spectrum (influenza only), GI side effects, resistance concerns, and modest benefit if started late.
